items.title: 보의연, 병원들에 '19종 실측' 조사 공문…에이아이트릭스 "고시 위반 아니다"
items.excerpt: Following a National Assembly audit, Korea's NECA sent a written survey to 171 hospitals that used AITRICS' VitalCare deterioration-prediction AI under the innovative-medical-technology reimbursement pathway, asking whether all 19 input variables were actually measured for every patient (deadline Nov 19); AITRICS says imputing missing values is within its MFDS approval.
items.rationale: Concrete regulator action on a reimbursed clinical AI: NECA audits 171 hospitals' use of VitalCare inputs, with the vendor disputing the reading.

items.title: As more doctors consult chatbots, health systems can block them — or buy in
items.excerpt: Health systems are split on clinicians' use of consumer AI tools like OpenEvidence: Monument Health blocked it after finding a doctor had stored more than 100 patient records in the tool, while others are licensing HIPAA-compliant versions.
items.rationale: Patient-privacy incident driving a concrete hospital policy choice (block vs license) on clinician chatbot use.

items.title: 모니터 대신 환자 눈 맞춘다…정신과·소청과 호평 AI 차팅 '니어닥'
items.excerpt: AI EMR charting assistant Neardoc (Studio Kiko), which drafts SOAP notes from doctor-patient conversation in real time and learns each physician's charting style, is drawing strongest uptake in psychiatry and pediatrics; Bosa reports ~500 clinics and 970,000 visit records since its May launch, with self-reported chart time falling from 3m48s to 1m08s per visit.
items.rationale: Freshest item in the pool: real clinic adoption numbers for an AI scribe, with specialty-level uptake and charting-time data.

items.title: Quibim's prostate MRI AI joins Microsoft imaging AI network
items.excerpt: FDA-cleared QP-Prostate, which detects suspected lesions on biparametric prostate MRI, is now available through Microsoft's Precision Imaging Network, with results delivered into PowerScribe for radiologists to review before finalizing reports.
items.rationale: An FDA-cleared prostate MRI tool lands inside radiologists' reporting workflow (PowerScribe) — a deployment change, not just a deal.

items.title: Beyond skin deep: physiologic oral pigmentation as an overlooked validation gap in AI-assisted oral cancer screening
items.excerpt: AI oral cancer screening tools such as MeMoSA have been validated almost exclusively in Asian populations; the authors argue physiologic oral pigmentation, which varies by race, may cause classifiers to flag normal variation as suspicious and call for targeted validation before wider deployment.
items.rationale: Patient-safety and bias angle: a specific, testable validation gap in oral cancer screening AI before broader rollout.

dedup.note: Dropped as duplicates: Cardiovascular Business Cleerly PARAMOUNT (same AHA trial already ran 11-09 via cleerly.com press); MedCity News NEJM LLM cost-of-care study (same NEJM AI paper ran 10-17); Radiology Business AI-derived FAI inflammation score (same Oxford/Antoniades coronary-inflammation running story as 10-27 Cardiovascular Business; also judged a likely repeat in the 11-15 run). Not picked for strength/diversity (not duplicates): Comm Med AML febrile-neutropenia model (thematically close to 11-13 persistent-fever item), npj bladder LLM benchmark, Radpair/Novarad partnership, STAT men's chatbot feature, JAMA rogue-agent Viewpoint, Medigate med-school AI conference, KBR GI-308 patent filing. Cross-section: no pick's product/event (AITRICS VitalCare NECA survey, Monument Health/OpenEvidence block, Neardoc, Quibim QP-Prostate, oral pigmentation) appears in the 30-day medicine history; published_urls.json could not be grepped (Read-only tools), so the orchestrator should exact-grep the five URLs before roll.
